title: Impact of Mobile Phone Coverage on Market Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS)
- Why: Mobile adoption (x) is likely endogenous to market prices (y) due to reverse causality and omitted variables (e.g., economic activity). Topographic suitability (z) affects the cost and feasibility of mobile infrastructure but should not directly affect prices except through mobile adoption, making it a plausible instrument.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: z is correlated with x conditional on controls (strong first stage).
  - Exclusion: z affects y only through x, not directly or through omitted channels (conditional on controls).
  - Independence: Conditional on controls, z is as-good-as-random with respect to unobservables affecting y.
  - Monotonicity: No defiers in adoption with respect to z.
  - Interpretation: Under these, the 2SLS identifies the LATE of mobile adoption on prices for compliers.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Package setup
pkg_needed <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest", "readr")
for (p in pkg_needed) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(readr)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s76_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Ensure correct types
df$y <- as.numeric(df$y)
df$x <- as.numeric(df$x)
df$z <- as.numeric(df$z) # binary {0,1}
df$controls <- as.numeric(df$controls)

# 2) Descriptives (optional, not printed extensively)
n <- nrow(df)

# 3) OLS (naive)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_vcov <- vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols, vcov = ols_vcov)
beta_ols <- coef(ols)["x"]
se_ols <- sqrt(diag(ols_vcov))["x"]
t_ols <- beta_ols / se_ols
p_ols <- 2 * pt(abs(t_ols), df = n - length(coef(ols)), lower.tail = FALSE)
ci_ols <- c(beta_ols - 1.96 * se_ols, beta_ols + 1.96 * se_ols)

# 4) First stage and instrument strength
fs_full <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_restr <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
# Conventional partial F-stat for z in first stage
wt <- waldtest(fs_full, fs_restr)
F_fs <- as.numeric(wt$F[2])
p_fs <- as.numeric(wt$`Pr(>F)`[2])

# Robust (HC1) Wald test for z in first stage (reports Chi-sq; with 1 df it's comparable)
wt_rob <- waldtest(fs_full, fs_restr, vcov = vcovHC(fs_full, type = "HC1"))
Chi2_fs_rob <- as.numeric(wt_rob$Chisq[2])
p_fs_rob <- as.numeric(wt_rob$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])

# First-stage coefficient on z (with robust SE)
fs_ct <- coeftest(fs_full, vcov = vcovHC(fs_full, type = "HC1"))
beta_fs_z <- as.numeric(fs_ct["z", "Estimate"])
se_fs_z <- as.numeric(fs_ct["z", "Std. Error"])

# 5) Reduced form (effect of z on y)
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_ct <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))
beta_rf_z <- as.numeric(rf_ct["z", "Estimate"])
se_rf_z <- as.numeric(rf_ct["z", "Std. Error"])

# 6) 2SLS main specification
ivm <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(ivm, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(ivm, vcov = iv_vcov)
beta_iv <- as.numeric(iv_ct["x", "Estimate"])
se_iv <- as.numeric(iv_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
t_iv <- beta_iv / se_iv
# Using normal approx for CI
ci_iv <- c(beta_iv - 1.96 * se_iv, beta_iv + 1.96 * se_iv)
p_iv <- 2 * pnorm(abs(t_iv), lower.tail = FALSE)

# 7) Robustness check 1: add nonlinear control
df$controls_sq <- df$controls^2
ivm_nl <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls_sq | z + controls + controls_sq, data = df)
iv_nl_vcov <- vcovHC(ivm_nl, type = "HC1")
iv_nl_ct <- coeftest(ivm_nl, vcov = iv_nl_vcov)
beta_iv_nl <- as.numeric(iv_nl_ct["x", "Estimate"])
se_iv_nl <- as.numeric(iv_nl_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
ci_iv_nl <- c(beta_iv_nl - 1.96 * se_iv_nl, beta_iv_nl + 1.96 * se_iv_nl)

# 8) Robustness check 2: report reduced form and first-stage consistency
# Sign of RF(beta_z) and FS(beta_z) should match sign pattern of IV via Wald (beta_iv ≈ beta_rf_z / beta_fs_z)

wald_iv_from_rf_fs <- beta_rf_z / beta_fs_z

# 9) Print clear numerical results
cat("=== Main 2SLS Estimate (HC1-robust) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("beta_IV (effect of mobile adoption on prices): %.4f\n", beta_iv))
cat(sprintf("SE_IV (robust): %.4f\n", se_iv))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_iv[1], ci_iv[2]))
cat(sprintf("p-value (robust, normal approx): %.4f\n\n", p_iv))

cat("=== Instrument Strength (First Stage) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("First-stage coefficient on z: %.4f (SE robust: %.4f)\n", beta_fs_z, se_fs_z))
cat(sprintf("Partial F-stat (conventional): %.2f  (p=%.4f)\n", F_fs, p_fs))
cat(sprintf("Robust Wald Chi-sq (1 df): %.2f  (p=%.4f)\n\n", Chi2_fs_rob, p_fs_rob))

cat("=== Reduced Form (z -> y, HC1-robust) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("beta_RF(z on y): %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", beta_rf_z, se_rf_z))
cat(sprintf("Implied Wald estimator beta_RF / beta_FS: %.4f\n\n", wald_iv_from_rf_fs))

cat("=== OLS (naive, HC1-robust) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("beta_OLS: %.4f (SE: %.4f) | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f] | p=%.4f\n\n",
            beta_ols, se_ols, ci_ols[1], ci_ols[2], p_ols))

cat("=== Robustness: Nonlinear Controls in 2SLS (HC1-robust) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("beta_IV (with controls^2): %.4f (SE: %.4f) | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            beta_iv_nl, se_iv_nl, ci_iv_nl[1], ci_iv_nl[2]))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Greater mobile adoption should improve information flows, reduce search frictions and market power, and compress markups, lowering average consumer market prices.
- Magnitude: Moderate. Expect roughly -0.2 to -0.4 reduction in prices (in the dataset’s standardized units) per 1-unit increase in adoption, with IV more negative than OLS if positive endogeneity bias exists (e.g., higher prices drive adoption). Robustness with nonlinear controls should yield similar magnitude and sign.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use topographic suitability as an instrument for mobile adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased mobile adoption leads to a decrease in market prices.
